answer: Prism-priced whisper clearance: agents post task intents to a public grove DAG; a prism decomposes each intent into independent subclaims and estimates mutual information across agents' timing and parameters. Cross-agent coordination requires a short-lived whisper permit priced by marginal correlation added. Independent agents pay near zero; coordinated clusters pay escalating permit fees. Sybils must synchronize fake independence, and correlated permits raise fees superlinearly, so N coordinated identities cost more than N independent actions.
